references.text: The preceding verse describes how Gideon divided the three hundred men into three groups and gave them trumpets, empty jars with torches inside, setting the context for his instruction to watch him and do the same.
The following verse continues Gideon's instructions and shows what will happen when he and his men blow the trumpets, which is the direct continuation of his command to follow his example.
Paul urges the Corinthians to imitate him as he imitates Christ, a similar principle of leadership by example that Gideon demonstrates when he says 'watch me and do the same'.
Paul urges the Philippians to imitate him and follow the example of those who walk as he does, reflecting Gideon's principle of leading by example.
Moses instructs Israel that the Lord goes before them in battle, a similar theme of divine leadership in war seen in Gideon's strategy.
Joshua gives detailed instructions to the people before the conquest of Jericho, similar to Gideon's precise instructions to his men before the attack on the Midianite camp.
